tierWindow.goal: Run a piece of research with rigour and ethical integrity: design it ethically, handle its data responsibly, and sustain research integrity from the proposal through to the dissertation.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Application, evaluation and justification (apply, evaluate, justify, anticipate, defend). The learner transfers principles to decisions about their own research.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Ill-defined, multi-factor judgements in which ethical principles are weighed against practical constraints, with competing considerations held together.
tierWindow.autonomy: Low scaffolding; the learner is addressed as a researcher making defensible decisions. Feedback probes reasoning rather than confirming recall.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner is an advanced student, typically undertaking or about to undertake a substantial piece of their own research such as a dissertation or master's project. They have already shaped a project and know the research-document genres (the work of this pathway's introductory and intermediate tiers). Ethics, data handling and rigour are treated as things they must own and defend as a researcher, not meet for the first time.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, research ethics and integrity: the principles that govern sound research and how approval is secured. Second, handling research data responsibly: the duties you owe the people who provide your data. Third, rigour across the research project: sustaining integrity from proposal to dissertation. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This course is about conducting research well: running a project with rigour and holding it to ethical and academic integrity. By the end you will be able to justify the principles that govern ethical research, handle participant data responsibly, and sustain integrity and rigour across a project from proposal to dissertation.

As an advanced student you are undertaking, or about to undertake, your own substantial research, where these are decisions you must make and defend rather than rules to recall.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: justify the ethical principles, handle data responsibly, sustain integrity and rigour across the project.

practiceConnection.academic: Running research with integrity is what separates work that can be trusted from work that merely looks finished. Every ethics application you complete, every participant whose data you protect, and every decision you can defend to an examiner draws on the same habits.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: This is the advanced tier of the pathway, so there is no deeper course to climb to. Going wider, the same rigour and integrity underpin Academic Writing, Criticality and Referencing, where you put these habits to work on related tasks.
decidedValue.whereNextOmitReason: wrapper-close/where-next is excluded at the advanced tier by the skeleton (generate-course-shell.js: included unless facetSet.tier === 'advanced'); the block is not realised in the built course.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Conducting research well is now something you can describe and defend. You can justify the ethical principles that govern a project and explain how approval is secured, treating the ethics form as the substance of integrity rather than a hurdle. You can handle participant data responsibly, protecting confidentiality, securing consent and preserving anonymity. And you can sustain integrity and rigour across a whole project, so that proposal, method and dissertation tell one coherent story.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, rigour and ethics are things you practise in every piece of research you undertake. Each ethics application, each dataset you protect, each decision you can account for, is this habit at work. It is also what research and professional practice reward most: work whose integrity can be shown, not just asserted.
